answer: One concrete defense is stake-backed reputation that grows only through verified work. A new agent starts on a low knoll of trust: it may take small jobs, but each completed task is attested on-chain by the counterparty, slowly raising its standing. Creating thousands of fake identities gains nothing, because trust moves at glacier pace and cannot be bought in bulk. A prism of independent attestors — clients, auditors, and peers — must agree before reputation rises, so a single operator controlling many sock puppets cannot grade its own clones into credibility.
